title: Excessive collection of identifying attributes during registration
description: The registration flow collects multiple direct identifiers and sensitive attributes together—email, full name, government ID, and a six-digit code—creating a rich identity record at account creation. If all are not strictly necessary for authentication, the process may expose more identity information than needed and increase privacy impact from misuse or breach.
assumptions: Assumes the authentication service stores or processes all listed fields as part of registration and that some may be optional or not strictly necessary for initial account creation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; I am confident about the identifiability threat but not fully certain that 'I.1' is the exact LINDDUN Pro node label.

title: Registration attributes enable linkage across services or records
description: Email address, full name, and especially government ID can serve as stable correlators, allowing records created in this system to be linked with other databases or future transactions involving the same parent. This increases the risk that activity in this service can be connected to the same individual elsewhere.
assumptions: Assumes the collected identifiers are retained or reused beyond the single registration transaction.
uncertainty_note: Threat applicability is strong, but the specific node id 'L.1' is an approximate best match from memory.

title: Sensitive registration data may be disclosed in transit or at intake
description: The flow carries credentials and highly sensitive personal data, including password and government ID. If transport protection, endpoint hardening, logging controls, or secure input handling are weak, these values could be exposed to network observers, intermediaries, support personnel, or application logs.
assumptions: Assumes there is some possibility of inadequate TLS, insecure logging, or weak handling at the receiving process.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; the disclosure threat is clear even if the exact subtree label differs in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Parent may be unable to prove or contest submitted registration details
description: If the service does not provide verifiable confirmation of what registration data was submitted and when, the parent may later be unable to demonstrate that certain details were entered correctly, or may be unable to repudiate a registration they did not intend to complete. This is especially relevant for sensitive fields such as government ID.
assumptions: Assumes lack of user-visible confirmation, signed receipts, or trustworthy audit evidence presented back to the user.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is somewhat context-dependent for this flow, so applicability is moderate and the node id is a best-effort estimate.

title: Users may be unaware of why government ID and code are collected
description: At registration, the parent may not understand why each field is required, how the government ID and six-digit code will be used, whether they are mandatory, how long they will be retained, or with whom they may be shared. Insufficient notice undermines informed consent and user awareness.
assumptions: Assumes the interface does not clearly explain purpose, necessity, retention, and sharing for each field.
uncertainty_note: Threat is likely applicable, but the exact LINDDUN Pro node id under Unawareness may differ.

title: Collection may exceed purpose limitation or data minimization requirements
description: Collecting government ID during initial account registration may be unnecessary or disproportionate for the stated purpose of authentication unless there is a clear legal or operational basis. This raises non-compliance risk with privacy principles such as data minimization, purpose limitation, and lawful basis/transparency obligations.
assumptions: Assumes no demonstrated necessity or legal basis has yet been established for collecting government ID and the six-digit code at this stage.
uncertainty_note: This is a strong non-compliance concern, but the exact LINDDUN Pro node id is an approximate best guess.

title: Registration flow may not support data subject rights over submitted identity data
description: If the authentication service lacks mechanisms to let the parent access, correct, or delete submitted registration data such as name, email, or government ID, the individual may be unable to exercise control over their data after submission. The risk is heightened because the collected data is sensitive and identity-bearing.
assumptions: Assumes the system may store registration inputs without adequate rights-management or self-service correction/deletion capabilities.
uncertainty_note: The detectability/non-compliance boundary can be blurry here; I am using Dd for lack of control/data rights with approximate node mapping.

title: Excessive storage of parent account attributes
description: The parent account record may include more personal data than necessary for authentication or account management, leading to unnecessary disclosure risk if the users collection is queried, breached, or repurposed.
assumptions: The flow stores a full parent account profile, not just the minimum fields strictly required for authentication.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for detectability/disclosure from data storage; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: Sensitive account data stored without adequate protection
description: If the parent account data is written to MongoDB without strong protection such as encryption at rest, field-level protection, or strict access control, an attacker or over-privileged insider could learn personal details from the users collection.
assumptions: The users collection contains personal identifiers, contact details, credentials metadata, or other sensitive parent-account information.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best match for disclosure through insufficient protection of stored data.

title: Parent accounts linkable across records and services
description: Storing a stable internal identifier, email address, phone number, or shared account key in the users collection can make the same parent identifiable across multiple records, sessions, or connected services, enabling linkage of activities and profiles.
assumptions: The stored parent account includes persistent identifiers reused elsewhere in the system.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for linkability due to persistent identifiers in stored account data.

title: Parent directly identifiable from stored account record
description: The users collection may store direct identifiers such as name, email address, phone number, postal address, or payment-related details that allow a parent to be directly identified from the record.
assumptions: The parent account contains one or more direct identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for identifiability through direct identifiers in the datastore.

title: Parent account stored without data minimization or purpose limitation
description: The system may store parent account data in MongoDB without demonstrating that each attribute is necessary for the stated purpose of authentication/account creation, creating non-compliance with privacy principles such as minimization and purpose limitation.
assumptions: Some stored attributes may exceed what is required to create and manage the account.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; mapped to non-compliance with privacy principles around minimization and purpose limitation.

title: Lack of retention limits for parent account data
description: If parent account records are retained indefinitely in the users collection after they are no longer needed, the storage may violate retention and storage-limitation obligations and increase long-term privacy risk.
assumptions: No defined deletion or archival policy exists for obsolete parent accounts.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-compliance related to retention; exact subnode may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Insufficient user awareness of what parent data is stored
description: Parents may not understand which personal attributes are written to the users collection, for what purpose, and for how long, reducing transparency and informed expectations about the handling of their account data.
assumptions: Privacy notice, just-in-time notice, or UI disclosures may be incomplete or unclear.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; mapped to unawareness regarding collection/storage practices.

title: JWT enables cross-context linkability of parent sessions
description: If the JWT contains a stable subject identifier, account id, device id, or other persistent claims, the Parent User or any relying component that sees the token can link multiple sessions and interactions belonging to the same person across time and possibly across services.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is visible to the parent client and contains stable identifiers or correlatable claims.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a best-fit for linkability via persistent identifiers in a message; exact node naming may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: User data in authentication response may reveal excessive identity information
description: Returning user data together with the JWT may disclose more identifying attributes than necessary to the Parent User endpoint or to anyone with access to the client side, such as full name, email, internal user id, role, or family relationship details.
assumptions: Assumes the payload includes personal attributes beyond what is strictly needed to establish the session.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit identity disclosure node; exact node id may differ across threat-tree editions.

title: Authentication response discloses personal data to unintended observers
description: JWTs and attached user data can expose personal data if intercepted in transit, logged by intermediaries, stored in browser history, or exposed through client-side debugging, especially if the token embeds readable claims rather than opaque references.
assumptions: Assumes possible exposure through transport metadata, logs, client storage, or token contents readable without additional protection.
uncertainty_note: Selected as a generic data disclosure node for personal data exposure on a data flow; exact subtree mapping may vary.

title: Authentication response reveals unnecessary personal-data content
description: Combining a JWT with user data may violate data minimization if more attributes, claims, or retention-enabling metadata are sent than are needed for the parent to authenticate and start a session.
assumptions: Assumes the design could instead use a smaller token or fetch needed attributes just-in-time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/data minimization style node under disclosure of information/content; exact LINDDUN Pro node id is uncertain.

title: Unreadable or opaque token handling may reduce parent awareness of data use
description: If the parent receives a JWT and bundled user data without clear indication of what claims are included, how long the token is valid, or how the data will be used and stored, the data subject may lack awareness and transparency about processing.
assumptions: Assumes limited notice in the client UX about token contents, purposes, or downstream sharing.
uncertainty_note: Using a best-fit unawareness node for insufficient transparency on this flow; exact node id may differ.

title: Bundled JWT and user data may exceed consent or stated purpose
description: Sending user profile data alongside the authentication token may process or disclose personal data beyond the purpose consented to by the parent, especially if optional attributes are included for convenience rather than necessity.
assumptions: Assumes consent, contract terms, or privacy notice limit processing to authentication/session establishment only.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node for purpose limitation or lawful-basis mismatch; exact node id may vary by taxonomy.

title: Repeated child login submissions may be linkable to the same child or household
description: The authentication service can link multiple login attempts containing the same parent email to one account, child, or household over time. This enables building a usage history of when the child logs in and from where.
assumptions: The same parent email is reused across sessions and login metadata such as time, IP address, or device characteristics are available to the service.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best fit for linkability at the authentication service, but exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may vary.

title: Parent email in child login can identify the child or household
description: Using a parent email address as a login identifier can directly or indirectly identify the child, parent, or household to the authentication service, especially when combined with existing account records.
assumptions: The authentication service stores or can access account data tied to the parent email.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit identifiability node; exact subnode id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Login attempts reveal that a child or parent uses the service
description: A successful or even attempted login discloses the involvement of a specific child account, parent email, or household with the service. Error behavior may also reveal whether the account exists.
assumptions: The service processes the parent email and can distinguish valid from invalid accounts; responses or internal records preserve this fact.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node; could also overlap with account enumeration style disclosure depending on the detailed threat tree.

title: Collection of parent email and password may exceed data minimization expectations for child access
description: The flow sends a parent email address and password when a child logs in. This may expose more personal data than necessary for the child to authenticate, especially if a child-specific pseudonymous credential could have been used instead.
assumptions: Alternative authentication designs are feasible, such as child-specific usernames, tokens, delegated parent consent artifacts, or pseudonymous identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/disclosure of information over-collection style node; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming for data minimization issues may differ.

title: Child may be unaware that parent credentials are being processed for authentication
description: The child user may not understand that the parent email and password are personal data being transmitted to and processed by the authentication service, nor how this affects privacy and account linkage.
assumptions: The interface and notices are aimed at account access rather than explaining data use in a child-comprehensible way.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node; exact subnode id is uncertain.

title: Use of parent credentials for child login may not align with child-data and consent obligations
description: Processing a parent email and password as part of a child login may create compliance risks if the purpose, legal basis, parental consent handling, retention, or transparency obligations for child-related data are not properly addressed.
assumptions: The system is subject to privacy requirements for children and account/authentication data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ based on the compliance taxonomy used.

title: Child profile data exposed to unintended viewers on the child device
description: The flow delivers child profiles together with a JWT to the Child User. If the child device or session is shared, unlocked, or observable by others, profile attributes can be disclosed to unauthorized parties. This is especially relevant because profile data may reveal personal characteristics or account structure.
assumptions: The child profiles contain personal data and are rendered or stored on the recipient side after delivery.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for information disclosure to an unauthorized recipient/viewer, but exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may differ.

title: JWT enables inference that the recipient is a child account
description: The JWT explicitly contains userType=child. Anyone with access to the token or its decoded claims can infer that the user is a child, which may reveal age-category status and potentially sensitive account segmentation information.
assumptions: JWT claims are readable by the client or by entities that can inspect the token in logs, browser storage, proxies, or on-device tools.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/inference node; exact subnode id may vary in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Stable JWT or profile identifiers can link child sessions and profiles across contexts
description: If the JWT or child profile payload contains stable identifiers, the child can be linked across sessions, devices, or services. This may permit correlation of the same child account over time and across different processing contexts.
assumptions: The token or profile data includes persistent identifiers such as subject IDs, profile IDs, or equivalent stable claims.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit linkability node for stable identifiers in a data flow; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Profile payload reveals behavioral or household context beyond authentication needs
description: Sending child profiles alongside the authentication token may reveal additional information such as number of profiles, names, avatars, preferences, or usage segmentation. Even if not directly identifying, these data can increase the detectability of the child's habits or household composition.
assumptions: Child profiles include metadata beyond the minimum required to complete login.
uncertainty_note: This is a best-fit detectability/inference-style node; exact node id may not match official LINDDUN Pro wording.

title: Excessive disclosure of child profile data may violate data minimization and child-privacy obligations
description: Bundling child profiles with the authentication response may send more personal data than is necessary for the immediate purpose of authentication. For child users, over-disclosure can conflict with privacy-by-default, data minimization, or special protections applicable to children's data.
assumptions: Authentication can succeed without transmitting the full child profile set, or a reduced payload would suffice.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance/data-minimization node; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode id may differ.

title: Insufficient evidence of what child-profile data was disclosed to the child session
description: If the service does not keep privacy-respecting records of which JWT claims and child profiles were returned, it may be difficult later to demonstrate what data was disclosed, to investigate complaints, or to support data-subject rights requests. This weakens accountability around disclosure of child data.
assumptions: Audit logging or disclosure records are absent or insufficiently detailed.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation-related node is a best estimate; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may differ.

title: Collection of directly identifying child data
description: The flow includes the child's name and government ID, which directly identify the child and can enable identity-related misuse if intercepted, over-collected, or accessed beyond the stated purpose of profile creation.
assumptions: The child profile is intended for account/profile setup and not all recipients or downstream uses of these identifiers are necessarily required for that purpose.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-effort; using a generic identifiability node because exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may vary.

title: Indirect identification via quasi-identifiers
description: Date of birth and gender, especially when combined with name and government ID, increase the ability to single out and identify the child even in datasets where direct identifiers are later removed.
assumptions: The system may store or reuse subsets of these attributes in contexts beyond the initial submission.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for indirect identifiability / singling out; exact subnode may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Disclosure of sensitive child personal data in transit or at intake
description: This flow carries highly sensitive personal data about a child, including government ID and date of birth. Unauthorized disclosure during transmission, logging, debugging, or initial processing could expose the child's identity and enable fraud or other harms.
assumptions: The data may traverse networks, intermediaries, client telemetry, or application logs before secure storage controls apply.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort generic disclosure node; exact node id may vary depending on whether LINDDUN Pro distinguishes transfer, storage, and processing disclosures.

title: Linkability of child profile to other records and services
description: The combination of name, date of birth, gender, and government ID creates a strong linkage key that can connect the child profile to other internal accounts, parental records, educational, healthcare, or third-party datasets.
assumptions: The organization or partners may possess overlapping attributes in other systems.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort generic linkability node; exact subnode may differ.

title: Excessive data disclosure relative to profile-creation purpose
description: Collecting a government ID, along with name, date of birth, and gender, for child profile creation may disclose more personal data than is necessary for the stated purpose, violating data minimization expectations.
assumptions: Government ID may not be strictly necessary to create a basic child profile; necessity depends on regulatory or verification requirements.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-effort for unnecessary / excessive disclosure; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may vary.

title: Unawareness of collection and downstream use of child's identifiers
description: The parent may not fully understand why each child attribute, especially government ID, is required, how long it will be retained, who it will be shared with, or whether it will be used for verification, analytics, or profiling.
assumptions: Privacy notices or just-in-time explanations may be absent, incomplete, or difficult to understand during profile creation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort generic unawareness node; exact subnode may differ.

title: Potential non-compliance with child-data protection and data minimization obligations
description: Processing child personal data and government ID during profile creation may conflict with legal obligations if the system lacks a valid basis, appropriate parental authorization handling, minimization, retention limits, or special protections for children's data.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy imposes heightened protections for children's data and government-issued identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort generic non-compliance node; exact node id may differ by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Insufficient evidence of parental submission and consent context
description: If the flow is not properly bound to the parent's authenticated identity, timestamp, notice version, and asserted authority to provide the child's data, the organization may be unable to prove what was submitted and under what consent or authorization context.
assumptions: The process may not capture auditable evidence for this submission event.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort generic non-repudiation node; in privacy contexts this is nuanced and exact mapping may differ.

title: Stored child profiles may be inferable by unauthorized parties
description: The childprofiles collection stores sensitive profile attributes about children. If access controls, query restrictions, or tenant/role separation are weak, an internal or external party could infer private facts about a child from stored records or update patterns.
assumptions: The collection may contain personal and potentially sensitive attributes, and more than one role or service can access the datastore.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Child profiles in the datastore may be disclosed
description: Storing or updating child profiles in MongoDB creates a risk of confidentiality breach through excessive read permissions, backup exposure, misconfiguration, injection, or compromised credentials, resulting in disclosure of children's personal data.
assumptions: MongoDB records, replicas, backups, or admin interfaces are reachable by multiple components or operators.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Users may be insufficiently informed about storage or updates of child profiles
description: When the system stores or updates a child profile, the data subject or guardian may not be adequately informed about what attributes are stored, why updates occur, how long records are retained, and who can access them.
assumptions: Transparency notices may be incomplete or detached from the actual storage/update behavior.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ. This is a flow-related transparency threat rather than a pure technical datastore flaw.

title: Storage of child profiles may exceed consent, purpose, or legal basis
description: The store/update operation may write attributes for a child profile without valid parental consent, beyond the stated purpose, for excessive retention, or in a way that conflicts with children's privacy obligations and applicable data protection requirements.
assumptions: The application processes children's data and may rely on consent, contract, or legitimate-interest constraints.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Child records may be linkable across contexts via persistent identifiers
description: If the child profile collection stores stable identifiers or shared keys, records can be linked across sessions, services, households, or datasets, enabling broader profiling of a child than intended.
assumptions: Profiles include persistent identifiers or combinations of quasi-identifiers that are reused elsewhere.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Stored child profiles may allow identification of a child
description: Direct identifiers or rich combinations of attributes in the childprofiles collection may make a child identifiable, even if some fields are partially masked or pseudonymized.
assumptions: Profiles include direct identifiers or sufficiently unique attribute combinations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Profile changes may be performed without adequate evidence or accountability
description: If the process updates child profiles without robust audit trails, timestamps, actor identity, or change justification, parties may later be unable to prove who created or modified a profile and under what authority, undermining accountability and dispute resolution.
assumptions: The process performs write/update actions and audit logging may be incomplete or mutable.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Search, request, like, and comment events can be linked to the same child profile
description: Repeated video searches, requests, likes, and comments sent from the child user to the video management service can be correlated over time to build a persistent behavioral profile. This may reveal interests, routines, emotional state, and social interaction patterns of a child.
assumptions: The service can associate multiple requests with the same account, device, IP address, cookie, or other identifier.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Child identity may be inferred from video interaction content and metadata
description: Search terms, requested videos, likes, and especially comment text may contain direct or indirect identifiers that allow the service to identify the child or distinguish them from other users. Metadata such as account identifiers or device-level identifiers can further enable identification.
assumptions: Requests include account, session, device, or network metadata, or comments/searches may contain personal details.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Sensitive attributes about a child can be detected from searches and engagement
description: The service can infer sensitive traits or states from the child's searches, requested videos, likes, and comments, such as health concerns, religious interests, political exposure, learning difficulties, fears, sexuality-related curiosity, or other age-sensitive characteristics.
assumptions: The service stores or analyzes interaction histories and content semantics.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Interactions may disclose private interests or personal information beyond what the child expects
description: Free-text comments and detailed search/request histories can disclose private interests, opinions, or personal circumstances to the service, especially if the child overshares in comments or searches for sensitive topics.
assumptions: The service receives and can inspect full query strings and comment content.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Child may be unaware of collection and secondary use of interaction data
description: A child may not understand that every search, request, like, and comment is collected, retained, analyzed, and potentially used for personalization, recommendation, moderation, profiling, or sharing with third parties. This limits meaningful awareness and user control.
assumptions: Privacy notices are complex, not child-friendly, or not presented contextually at the time of interaction.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Processing of a child's interaction data may lack valid consent or exceed allowed purposes
description: The service may process the child's searches, requests, likes, and comments without age-appropriate notice, verifiable parental consent where required, valid legal basis, purpose limitation, or retention limits. This creates risk of non-compliance with child privacy obligations.
assumptions: The user is a child and the service is subject to child-data protections or similar privacy regulation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Child may be unable to plausibly deny a like or comment later
description: If the service logs likes, comments, and requests together with timestamps and account/session identifiers, the child may later be unable to deny having performed a particular action. This can have social or disciplinary consequences, especially for comments.
assumptions: The service maintains attributable logs of user interactions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Metadata and stored video content may reveal sensitive personal information
description: Storing video metadata together with references to or embedded video files can expose personal information such as uploader identity, subjects appearing in videos, location, timestamps, device identifiers, titles, tags, and inferred behavioral patterns if the datastore is accessed by unauthorized parties or over-broadly queried.
assumptions: DS3 stores or indexes metadata that can be linked to individuals, and may also contain pointers to video files or combined records that reveal personal context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on generic information disclosure from stored personal data; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Records in the videos collection may enable linkage across uploads, users, and viewing contexts
description: Persistent identifiers, account IDs, device IDs, file hashes, tags, and timestamps in the videos collection can allow multiple records to be linked together, enabling construction of user profiles or correlation of activity across sessions, channels, or services.
assumptions: The collection contains stable identifiers or quasi-identifiers across multiple video records.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability via persistent record identifiers.

title: Queryable metadata may enable inference of private attributes
description: Even if direct identifiers are minimized, combinations of metadata fields such as upload time, geolocation, category, transcript-derived tags, and engagement indicators may allow inference of sensitive attributes about uploaders or data subjects in videos.
assumptions: Stored metadata includes enough attributes for indirect inference or analytics.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to capture inferential disclosure from combinations of stored metadata.

title: Insufficient proof of video metadata/file storage actions
description: If Video Management Service writes, updates, or deletes records in MongoDB without tamper-evident audit trails, parties may later deny having stored, changed, or removed specific video metadata or associated files, undermining accountability for privacy-relevant processing.
assumptions: Audit logging or integrity protection for write operations may be absent or incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation gaps around data storage actions.

title: Stored video records may identify individuals directly or indirectly
description: Video metadata and associated file references may contain names, usernames, thumbnails, voice/face references, exact timestamps, or other direct and indirect identifiers that make uploaders or recorded individuals identifiable from the datastore contents.
assumptions: Records include direct identifiers or combinations of quasi-identifiers sufficient for identification.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from stored records.

title: Video data may be stored beyond stated purpose or legal basis
description: The flow stores and retrieves video metadata and files in a combined datastore context, creating risk that personal data is retained, reused, or indexed for purposes broader than originally specified, or without a valid legal basis, consent scope, or retention limit.
assumptions: Purpose limitation, retention rules, or lawful-basis enforcement may not be technically enforced at storage time.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to capture non-compliance with purpose limitation, lawful basis, or retention obligations.

title: Users may be unaware that extensive video metadata and files are stored and reused
description: Data subjects and uploaders may not understand the scope of storage, indexing, retrieval, and secondary use of video metadata and associated files, particularly where derived metadata or internal retrieval features are not transparent.
assumptions: Notice and transparency mechanisms may not fully describe all stored fields and downstream uses.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency around storage and reuse.

title: Inability to delete or fully dissociate video data from related metadata
description: When metadata and files are stored in a combined or tightly linked manner, deleting a video may leave orphaned metadata, backups, thumbnails, indexes, or derived records, preventing effective deletion or dissociation of personal data.
assumptions: Deletion may not propagate consistently across linked storage artifacts, indexes, and backups.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability/disclosure-by-persistence issues around incomplete deletion; exact subtree may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Excessive retention of child search and watch history in profile management
description: The process stores detailed child search and watch history, which can reveal interests, habits, routines, and potentially sensitive inferences over time. If the process persists more history than necessary or retains it indefinitely, it enables profiling beyond the original purpose.
assumptions: The flow stores granular event history tied to an individual child profile rather than only short-lived aggregated recommendations data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for data over-collection/over-retention in processing; exact subtree label may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Secondary use of stored child history for profiling or analytics
description: Once search and watch history is stored in the childprofiles collection, it may be reused for analytics, behavior profiling, personalization, or other purposes beyond the immediate child-profile-management function. Such repurposing discloses more personal data than users may expect and increases privacy impact.
assumptions: Stored history is accessible to other internal services, analysts, or downstream recommendation/marketing functions.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for use beyond purpose / function creep; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may differ.

title: Identifiability of a child through persistent profile history
description: Search and watch history linked to a persistent child profile can make the child uniquely identifiable within the system, even if direct identifiers are limited. Distinctive viewing and search patterns can single out one child account over time.
assumptions: History records are associated with a stable child profile or account key and are queryable over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from stored records; exact node id may differ by catalog version.

title: Linkability of child activities across sessions and content interactions
description: Persistently storing search and watch history in one collection enables linking multiple activities, sessions, and interests to the same child profile. This creates a longitudinal behavioral record and increases privacy risk from comprehensive activity correlation.
assumptions: Events across multiple sessions are stored under a common profile identifier or otherwise correlated in the datastore.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability across records/sessions; exact node id may vary.

title: Users may be unaware that detailed child history is being stored
description: Parents or guardians may not realize that the system stores detailed child search and watch history in the profile datastore, especially if collection occurs automatically during normal use. Lack of visibility reduces meaningful user awareness and control.
assumptions: The interface does not clearly communicate the granularity, retention period, and uses of stored child history.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for insufficient user awareness/transparency; exact subtree id may differ.

title: Storing child behavior history may exceed consent or child-privacy expectations
description: Recording and persisting child search and watch history may be inconsistent with parental consent, age-appropriate defaults, or data minimization obligations for children's data. If the process stores this information without an appropriate legal basis or control, it creates non-compliance risk.
assumptions: The system is subject to child-data protection obligations and may require explicit parental authorization or strict minimization.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for missing legal basis/consent or non-compliant processing; exact node id may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Lack of evidence for consent and history changes affecting repudiation
description: If the datastore does not preserve reliable records of when child history was stored, updated, deleted, or collected under consent, the service may be unable to prove compliant handling, while users may be unable to contest or verify disputed processing. This weakens accountability around the stored profile history.
assumptions: Auditability and consent/provenance metadata are not separately maintained for writes into the childprofiles collection.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for insufficient evidence/accountability supporting non-repudiation; exact node may differ.

title: Exposure of child's or family's identity through uploaded video content
description: The uploaded video may contain direct identifiers or highly identifying attributes of the child or family, such as faces, voices, home interior, school uniforms, location cues, or spoken names. If the Video Management Service stores, processes, or routes this content without adequate minimization and access controls, the parent or child can be identified from the video.
assumptions: The uploaded video can contain personal data and may be retained or viewed by staff or downstream systems during approval/rejection.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may differ.

title: Linkability of multiple uploads to the same parent or child
description: Metadata and account context around video upload and moderation can allow multiple videos to be linked to the same parent user, child, household, device, or account over time. This may reveal behavior patterns or create a richer profile than necessary for approval/rejection.
assumptions: The service associates uploads with an account, session, device, or persistent identifier.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may vary; chosen as a best-fit generic linkability node.

title: Inference of sensitive family attributes from video and moderation outcome
description: Reviewers or systems may infer sensitive information from the uploaded video, such as health conditions, religion, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, precise home location, daily routines, or the child's age and school. Approval or rejection outcomes may further encode judgments about the family or child.
assumptions: Uploaded videos are reviewed by humans or automated systems and may contain contextual background details.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact inference subtree numbering may differ.

title: Parent cannot prove what video was submitted or what moderation decision was made
description: If the service does not provide reliable receipts, timestamps, hashes, or audit logs for uploads and decisions, the parent may be unable to demonstrate which video was submitted, when it was received, or whether it was approved or rejected. This can undermine accountability for privacy-impacting moderation decisions.
assumptions: The service may lack tamper-evident submission and decision records visible to the user.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro node id uncertain; this is a best-fit non-repudiation threat.

title: Unawareness of how uploaded videos are used, retained, or shared during approval/rejection
description: The parent may not be sufficiently informed about who can view the uploaded video, whether automated analysis is used, how long the video and moderation metadata are retained, whether rejected videos are kept, or whether content is reused for training, quality assurance, or policy enforcement. This lack of transparency impairs informed privacy decision-making.
assumptions: Notices presented at upload may be incomplete, unclear, or not specific to moderation processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/disclosure-of-information-related transparency node from memory; exact numbering may differ.

title: Insufficiently informed or specific consent for processing uploaded videos
description: If the parent uploads a video without clear, granular choice about moderation processing, retention, secondary use, or sharing with moderators/processors, consent or another permission basis may not be valid or sufficiently specific. This is especially sensitive where the video contains a child and third parties appearing in the recording.
assumptions: The system relies on consent or user agreement for at least part of the video-processing lifecycle.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro node id uncertain; selected as a best-fit unawareness/non-compliance-related consent node.

title: Processing of uploaded videos beyond necessity or legal basis
description: The Video Management Service may process more personal data than necessary for approval/rejection, retain videos longer than justified, or use them for incompatible secondary purposes such as analytics, model training, or broader content profiling. Such processing could violate purpose limitation, data minimization, retention, or child-data protection requirements.
assumptions: The service stores uploaded videos and related moderation metadata, potentially beyond the immediate approval workflow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node from memory; exact subtree numbering may differ.

title: Viewing-history linkability across sessions or devices
description: Streaming approved videos from the service to the child can create identifiers or stable session metadata that let observations of multiple viewing events be linked together, revealing a persistent viewing profile for the child across sessions or devices.
assumptions: The stream or related telemetry uses persistent identifiers, cookies, account tokens, device IDs, or other stable metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary depending on whether linkage arises from protocol metadata, account identifiers, or embedded telemetry.

title: Child identifiable through stream delivery metadata
description: The delivered video stream may expose identifying information about the child, such as account identifiers, device identifiers, IP address correlation, or personalized URLs/tokens, allowing the child to be identified by network observers or downstream parties.
assumptions: The streaming path, CDN, or player requests include unique tokens or metadata tied to the child or household.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability via observed attributes in the flow.

title: Disclosure of the child's video consumption to unauthorized parties
description: If the stream is observable by unauthorized recipients, network intermediaries, shared devices, or co-located users, the specific approved videos watched by the child may be disclosed, revealing preferences, habits, age-related inferences, or sensitive interests.
assumptions: The stream content, titles, thumbnails, request paths, or player metadata can be seen by parties beyond the intended child.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node; exact subnode depends on whether disclosure is of content, metadata, or viewing events.

title: Insufficient awareness of streaming-related data processing
description: The child or guardian may not be adequately informed that streaming the approved video involves collection or sharing of playback telemetry, device data, or CDN/logging information, reducing their awareness of how personal data is processed during delivery.
assumptions: Notices are absent, incomplete, or not presented in a child-appropriate and guardian-accessible way.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/unawareness node; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may differ.

title: Unexpected secondary use of viewing telemetry
description: Telemetry generated while streaming approved videos may be used for analytics, recommendations, profiling, experimentation, or ad-related purposes beyond the expectation of simply delivering the video to the child.
assumptions: Playback events, watch duration, pauses, rewinds, and device/network data are reused beyond core delivery.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance/unawareness-adjacent node for policy/expectation mismatch; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: Streaming to a child without meeting child-privacy obligations
description: Delivering video streams to a child may involve processing personal data such as device identifiers, viewing history, and telemetry without satisfying applicable child-privacy requirements, such as parental consent, data minimization, retention limits, or appropriate safeguards.
assumptions: The service is subject to child-specific privacy regulation or platform policy obligations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact subnode depends on the governing obligation and jurisdiction.

title: AI engine can link child browsing data to persistent child profiles
description: Browsing data retrieved from the childprofiles collection may contain stable identifiers or profile attributes that allow the AI Recommendation Engine to link events to a specific child over time, enabling detailed longitudinal profiling.
assumptions: The collection contains persistent child identifiers, account references, device identifiers, or sufficiently unique behavioral/profile attributes.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability via identifiers/profile data; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: AI engine may infer sensitive traits about a child from browsing history
description: Once child browsing data is ingested, the AI Recommendation Engine may derive interests, vulnerabilities, developmental stage, health-related concerns, religion, or other sensitive characteristics that were not explicitly provided, increasing privacy risk for minors.
assumptions: The recommendation model performs profiling or feature extraction from browsing behavior.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for inference from observed behavior; exact node id may differ in the official threat tree.

title: Child browsing records may disclose identifiable or highly personal information to the AI engine
description: The data flow may expose raw URLs, search terms, timestamps, clicked content, or embedded identifiers to the AI Recommendation Engine, revealing a child's habits and potentially direct or indirect identifiers.
assumptions: The transferred browsing data includes fine-grained event data rather than only aggregated signals.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for information disclosure in transit/processing context.

title: Using child browsing data for recommendations may exceed user or parent expectations
description: Repurposing stored child browsing data to train or drive an AI Recommendation Engine can create a mismatch between what children/parents expect the data to be used for and its actual use, especially if the use is only planned and not clearly communicated.
assumptions: Children or parents were not clearly informed that browsing data would be used for AI-driven personalization or model improvement.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for purpose/processing-use non-compliance or expectation mismatch; exact Dd subtree id may vary.

title: Processing child browsing data in the AI engine may lack valid consent or other lawful basis
description: Because the flow involves children's browsing data, sending it from the childprofiles collection to the AI Recommendation Engine may violate consent, parental authorization, purpose limitation, or data minimization requirements if not properly obtained and documented.
assumptions: The system is subject to privacy obligations for children's data and the planned AI use is not yet fully governed.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best approximation for non-compliance around consent/lawful basis and purpose limitation.

title: Children or parents may be unaware that browsing data is sent to the AI engine
description: If the transfer from the childprofiles collection to the AI Recommendation Engine is not transparently explained, data subjects may be unaware of the existence, scope, or consequences of this processing activity.
assumptions: Privacy notices, in-product explanations, or parental dashboards do not clearly describe this planned flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact U subtree id may differ.

title: Browsing data enables cross-context linkage by advertisers
description: Browsing data shared from the AI Recommendation Engine to third-party advertisers can be combined with advertisers' existing identifiers, cookies, device fingerprints, or partner datasets to link a user's activity across sites, apps, or services.
assumptions: Assumes the browsing data contains persistent identifiers, quasi-identifiers, or granular event patterns that advertisers can match to their own records.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best estimate for linkability via shared identifiers/patterns; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may differ.

title: Advertisers can infer sensitive interests from browsing data
description: Third-party advertisers receiving browsing data may infer sensitive attributes or interests, such as health concerns, political views, religion, sexual orientation, financial status, or other private traits, even if those attributes are not explicitly sent.
assumptions: Assumes browsing history/events are sufficiently detailed to support profiling or category inference.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for inferability from behavioral data; exact subnode may vary in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Browsing data may identify an individual or household
description: Browsing data sent to advertisers may directly or indirectly identify a person, device, or household when combined with IP address, cookie IDs, mobile ad IDs, account data, or unique browsing patterns.
assumptions: Assumes the flow includes direct identifiers, online identifiers, or sufficiently unique behavioral data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for identifiability of the data subject from transmitted data.

title: Planned sharing with advertisers may be unexpected to users
description: Users may not expect that their browsing data collected for recommendations is disclosed to unrelated third-party advertisers, making the data flow observable or discoverable in a way that surprises data subjects.
assumptions: Assumes users are not clearly informed at collection time about advertiser sharing, or the sharing is not obvious from the service context.
uncertainty_note: I am less confident in the precise discoverability/disclosure subnode; included because third-party sharing is often not apparent to users.

title: Secondary use of browsing data for advertising may be unaware or unclear
description: Browsing data originally collected to power recommendations may be repurposed for third-party advertising without users being sufficiently aware of the purpose, recipients, or implications of the sharing.
assumptions: Assumes notice is incomplete, consent is absent or ambiguous, or the purpose change is not made salient to users.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for unawareness about secondary use and third-party disclosure.

title: Sharing browsing data with advertisers may lack a valid legal basis or violate purpose limitation
description: Sending browsing data to third-party advertisers may be incompatible with the original collection purpose, exceed user consent, or fail applicable privacy-law requirements such as transparency, data minimization, or restrictions on sharing for targeted advertising.
assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to privacy/data-protection obligations and that advertiser sharing is planned but not yet fully governed.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for policy/legal non-compliance; exact subnode may differ by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Advertisers may deny receipt or downstream use of browsing data
description: If audit trails, contractual controls, or provenance records are insufficient, third-party advertisers could later deny having received specific browsing data, deny particular profiling actions, or deny onward sharing to other parties.
assumptions: Assumes weak logging, insufficient data-sharing agreements, or limited technical proof of transfer and processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-repudiation gaps in data transfer/processing accountability.

title: Stored government ID images can disclose highly sensitive personal data if accessed beyond need-to-know
description: Government ID images typically contain directly identifying and sensitive attributes such as full name, date of birth, document number, photograph, nationality, and address. Persisting these images in backend/uploads/ creates a risk that unauthorized internal users, compromised services, or attackers who gain file-system access can view or copy the images, resulting in disclosure of personal data.
assumptions: The file store is reachable by application components or administrators and contains raw image files rather than strongly protected derived artifacts only.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a generic stored-data disclosure node; exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node may vary.

title: Government ID images enable strong linkability across accounts, sessions, and systems
description: A stored ID image contains stable identifiers and biometric-like visual content that can be used to link the same individual across multiple accounts, verification attempts, or even external datasets. If the same file, document number, or image features are reused, records may be linked without the data subject's expectation.
assumptions: The system retains original images or identifiers long enough for cross-record comparison, deduplication, fraud checks, or later reuse.
uncertainty_note: Likely a linkability node related to correlating records via stable identifiers; exact sub-node id may differ.

title: Stored ID images make the individual directly identifiable
description: By storing a government-issued identity document image, the data subject becomes directly identifiable from the data itself. Anyone with access to the stored file can determine the person's identity without needing additional information.
assumptions: The uploaded images are legible and include standard identifying fields and a facial photograph.
uncertainty_note: Exact identifiability sub-node may differ; selected as a general direct-identification node.

title: Retention of raw government ID images in file storage may exceed necessity or legal basis
description: Storing full government ID images in backend/uploads/ may be unnecessary for the stated purpose if only verification results or limited attributes are needed. Continued retention of raw images can conflict with data minimization, storage limitation, or purpose limitation obligations, especially if no explicit retention policy or lawful basis covers this storage.
assumptions: The system stores raw images after verification and may not automatically delete or minimize them.
uncertainty_note: Mapped to a generic non-compliance/data-minimization-retention node; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary.

title: Users may be unaware that full ID images are being stored in backend file storage
description: If the service does not clearly inform users that uploaded government ID images are persisted in backend/uploads/, for how long, and for what secondary uses, individuals may not understand the extent of processing. This undermines transparency and user awareness about sensitive document handling.
assumptions: Privacy notices or just-in-time disclosures may be absent, incomplete, or not specific to raw image retention.
uncertainty_note: Chosen as a generic unawareness/transparency node; exact sub-node id may differ.

title: Lack of verifiable upload and storage logging may allow repudiation of ID-image handling actions
description: If Authentication Service does not create reliable audit records for when government ID images were uploaded, stored, accessed, or deleted, the service operator or users may later be unable to prove what happened to a specific document. This can impede accountability for sensitive personal-data handling.
assumptions: Audit trails for file writes, reads, and deletions may be incomplete, mutable, or not bound to actor identity.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central for this flow than disclosure/compliance; node id is an approximate generic non-repudiation node.

title: JWT in localStorage can expose user identity to scripts on the device
description: Storing a JWT in browser localStorage makes it accessible to any script executing in the page context, including injected or malicious third-party scripts. If the token contains identifiers or claims about the user, compromise of localStorage can disclose personal data and authenticated session context.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT contains identifying claims or can be used to retrieve user data, and that browser-side scripts may access localStorage.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for disclosure of stored data, but exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: Persistent localStorage token enables use beyond user expectations
description: localStorage persists across browser sessions until explicitly cleared. Users may believe authentication ends when closing the browser, yet the JWT can remain available and continue to re-authenticate the user later, creating processing beyond expected duration or context.
assumptions: Assumes the application reuses the stored JWT on later visits and users are not clearly informed of this persistence.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unexpected persistent reuse of data; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Storing JWT locally may exceed or obscure consent/choice about persistence
description: Persisting an authentication token in localStorage may occur without a clear user choice about storage duration, logout semantics, or device persistence. If users are not given meaningful control or informed consent regarding this client-side storage, the processing may be non-compliant with privacy expectations or policy.
assumptions: Assumes no explicit notice or consent mechanism exists for persistent client-side token storage.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is a compliance/consent concern tied to persistent browser storage.

title: Lack of auditable proof for client-side token retention and reuse
description: Once the authentication service issues a JWT for storage in localStorage, subsequent persistence, reuse, or deletion happen on the client side and may not be reliably visible to the service. This can make it hard to demonstrate whether a user remained logged in intentionally, logged out, or had a token retained on a shared device.
assumptions: Assumes limited server-side logging of token lifecycle events after issuance.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation-related applicability is weaker than disclosure here; included because client-side persistence can reduce provability of user actions. Exact node may differ.

title: Persistent JWT can facilitate linking of sessions on the same browser
description: A stable token stored in localStorage can act as a persistent identifier across visits, allowing the application or scripts with access to the browser storage to link multiple sessions and interactions to the same user or device over time.
assumptions: Assumes the token or associated subject claim remains stable across sessions and is reused.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via persistent identifier; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary.

title: Excessive disclosure of child history to parent
description: The child history returned for parent review may include more personal data than necessary for the parent's immediate purpose, such as sensitive events, detailed timestamps, or information about other individuals, causing unnecessary identifiability and exposure.
assumptions: The flow can contain detailed child history records rather than a minimized summary.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is a best-fit estimate for information disclosure due to over-broad data returned; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Disclosure to the wrong parent or unauthorized viewer
description: If the receiving parent user is not properly authenticated, authorized, or the session is mixed up, the child history could be exposed to someone who should not see it.
assumptions: Access control or session binding errors are possible at the point the parent views the returned history.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for unauthorized disclosure at the recipient side.

title: Linkability of child activities across contexts
description: The retrieved history may let the parent correlate the child's activities, events, or records across multiple contexts or time periods, enabling linkage of separate actions into a richer profile than intended.
assumptions: History aggregates data from multiple sources, dates, or activity contexts.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability from aggregated history; exact subnode uncertain.

title: Identifiability of child through detailed history
description: Even if some records are partially masked, combinations of events, dates, locations, or unique incidents in the child history may make the child readily identifiable or reveal sensitive traits.
assumptions: The history includes quasi-identifiers or unique event combinations.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for identifiability arising from data content.

title: Insufficient evidence of what child history was disclosed
description: If the process does not record what history was shown, to which parent account, and when, the organization may be unable to prove or contest whether a disclosure occurred, weakening accountability for privacy-relevant access.
assumptions: Audit logging of disclosures may be incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-repudiation/accountability gap; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Parent unaware of scope and sensitivity of returned history
description: The interface or response may not clearly communicate why specific child history elements are shown, how far back the history goes, or what inferences can be drawn, leading to unawareness about privacy impact and secondary use.
assumptions: The presentation lacks adequate transparency cues or explanations.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate for unawareness due to insufficient transparency in the returned data.

title: Sharing child history without valid legal basis or age-appropriate protections
description: Providing child history to a parent may violate applicable privacy requirements if consent, parental rights, custody limitations, child age/maturity considerations, or jurisdiction-specific rules are not properly handled.
assumptions: Applicable child-privacy, family-law, or data-protection obligations may restrict what can be shown to a parent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for policy/legal non-compliance; exact subnode uncertain because governing obligations are context-dependent.
